tail:
**Batch 19 authoring is complete.** The A page has six items, including a proved discrete-treatment identification theorem with its standard-Borel RCD formula. The B page has three verified examples: randomized assignment, binary confounding, and positivity failure.

The [batch manifest](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/statistical-models-experiments-62-batch-19.pages.json) records the item dependencies and levels. The [coverage record](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/statistical-models-experiments-62-batch-19.coverage.json) includes source locators, dispositions, retrieval history, and fetch stamps. Full text was read from [Hernán–Robins](https://miguelhernan.org/s/hernanrobins_WhatIf_19aug26.pdf), [Kang](https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~hyunseung/stat992_sp24/strong_ignorability.html), and [Aldous–Chewi](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/205B/chewi_notes.pdf). The old Hernán–Robins URL returned an HTML profile; I recovered the current author-hosted PDF and recorded that history.

The design and current plan-spec requirements agree. The [batch notes](/home/lazyinspirit/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/statistical-models-experiments-62-batch-19-notes.md) record how I reconciled the older dossier and audit evidence with current published suppliers.

Scoped checks passed: proof layout (9 items, 20 steps), precheck, strict proof contracts (9/9), dependency and manifest checks, focused dependency audits, content policy, rendercheck, and source fetch (3/3). All nine items have closed `ready` records. The run-wide readiness check remains open because other batches still have empty scaffolds. No unresolved prerequisite remains for batch 19.
